lessons.title: What day trading is, and the honest odds
points: A day trade opens and closes the same session. Nothing is held overnight, so an earnings report after the close cannot gap through your stop.
Most people who day trade lose money. Costs (spread, slippage, fees) are paid on every trade, win or lose, so a strategy has to beat them just to break even.
This pack never predicts. It reads charts, news and filings, does arithmetic, and checks your rules. You decide, and you own every order.
Paper trading is practice money on real prices. Stay on paper until weeks of results say the method holds up, and never trade money you cannot afford to lose.
lessons.example: On Wed Oct 28 2026 the daily scan matched 453 of 1,548 liquid charts. That is a list of charts that matched a rule, not 453 things to buy.
try: Ask: "is the market open" (/trader-alerts knows NYSE hours, holidays and early closes).

quiz.q: Why does a day trade avoid the risk of an overnight earnings gap?
choices: It is closed before the session ends
Stops always fill at their price
quiz.why: Flat by the close means no position is open when the report lands.

quiz.q: A scan finds 453 charts that match a setup. What are they?
choices: Stocks the scanner predicts will rise
Charts that matched a rule, to look at next
A ranked list of the best stocks
quiz.why: A setup is a pattern on a chart, not a prediction. You pick one to research, never all of them.

quiz.q: When is it reasonable to think about switching from paper to real money?
choices: After weeks of paper results you have reviewed
As soon as the bot is set up
quiz.why: One day proves nothing. A real sample of paper trades, reviewed honestly, is the minimum.

lessons.title: Candles, volume and the opening range
points: A bar (candle) has four prices for its time slot: open, high, low, close. A 5-minute bar from 9:30 covers 9:30 to 9:35 and is only complete at 9:35.
Volume is how many shares traded in the bar. A move on heavy volume has more participants behind it than one on thin volume.
The opening range is the high and low of the first 15 minutes (the 9:30, 9:35 and 9:40 bars). The first minutes are the noisiest of the day; the range lets the dust settle.
Never act on a bar that is still forming. Its close can change until the bar ends.
lessons.example: TSLA, Mon Oct 19 2026: the 9:30 to 9:40 bars made a range high of 362.18 and a low of 354.47. At 10:12 the 10:10 bar was still forming, so the entry timer said waiting.
try: After 9:50 AM ET ask: "did TSLA break its opening range?" (/trader-entry).

quiz.q: A 5-minute bar starts at 10:10. When is it complete?
quiz.why: A bar counts only once its full 5 minutes are over: start plus 5 minutes.

quiz.q: With a 15-minute opening range, which bars make the range?
choices: The last three bars of yesterday
quiz.why: Three 5-minute bars cover 9:30 to 9:45.

quiz.q: Why wait for the opening range instead of buying at 9:31?
choices: The first minutes are the noisiest and give no level to trade against
quiz.why: The range gives you a level (its high) and a place for a stop (its midpoint or low).

lessons.title: Setups: what the scanner looks for
points: 20-day closing-high breakout: the last close is above every close of the 20 sessions before it.
Bull flag: a strong run (over 10 % in 10 sessions) followed by 5 quiet closes inside a 5 % range.
Reclaim of the 20-day average: yesterday closed under its 20-day average, today closed above it.
Oversold: RSI 14 under 30. Oversold bounce: RSI was under 30 yesterday and today closed up. Oversold can stay oversold.
Opening-range breakout (ORB): during the session, the first completed 5-minute bar that CLOSES above the opening-range high.
lessons.example: Oct 28 2026: ORCL tagged 'reclaimed the 20-day average' after one 11 % day on its investor day. LPLA tagged 'oversold' after one 15 % drop on earnings. Same tags, very different stories: that is why news comes next.
try: Before the open ask: "find me setups" (/trader-scanner daily). After 9:50 AM: "opening range breakouts" (/trader-scanner orb).

quiz.q: What makes a chart an opening-range breakout in this pack?
choices: Any tick above the range high
A completed 5-minute bar that closes above the range high
quiz.why: A close, not a touch. Wicks above the high that close back inside do not count.

quiz.q: RSI 14 under 30 means the chart is...
choices: Oversold by that rule, which can last
quiz.why: Oversold describes the recent past. A falling stock can stay oversold for weeks.

quiz.q: Two stocks carry the same setup tag. What should you do before trading either?
quiz.why: ORCL and LPLA show a tag can come from very different news. /trader-news is the next step.

lessons.title: News and catalysts
points: Headlines are leads, not facts. Read the story or the filing before believing it.
Filings beat headlines. An 8-K is what the company told the SEC. Item 2.02 is earnings results, 5.02 an officer change, 1.03 bankruptcy, 4.02 past financials no longer reliable.
An earnings date inside your holding period is a gap risk: the price can jump past your stop at the next open.
A big move with no headline is worth noticing too. Somebody knows something, or it is noise; either way the risk is higher.
lessons.example: Thu Oct 29 2026 pre-market: HWM was up 3.4 % after its earnings 8-K (revenue $2.70B vs $2.59B expected). CVX and XOM report Fri Oct 30 before the open, so a CVX trade held overnight would carry that gap risk.
try: Ask: "any news on ORCL" or "morning briefing" (/trader-news).

quiz.q: A headline and the company's 8-K disagree. Which do you trust?
quiz.why: The 8-K is the company's own filing with the SEC.

quiz.q: A company reports earnings tomorrow before the open. Your plan is a day trade, flat by 3:55 PM today. Is the report a gap risk to this trade?
choices: No, the trade is closed before the report
Only if the stop is tight
quiz.why: Flat by the close keeps the trade out of tomorrow's opening gap.

quiz.q: An 8-K lists Item 4.02. What does that flag?
choices: Past financial statements should no longer be relied on
quiz.why: 4.02 is a non-reliance notice, a serious risk flag.

lessons.title: Timing the entry, and not chasing
points: The entry is the first completed bar that closes above the level. The entry timer says waiting, triggered, expired or not open yet.
No new entries before 9:45 AM or after your cutoff (15:30 by default). Late breakouts have less time to work before the close.
Do not chase. If the price is already well above the trigger, the stop is further away and the reward smaller. The bot skips triggers older than 6 minutes or more than 0.5 % above the trigger.
Long side only in this pack: it buys breakouts, it never sells short.
lessons.example: TSLA, Oct 19 2026: waiting at 10:12; triggered at 10:15 when the 10:10 bar closed at 364.18, 0.55 % over the 362.18 range high.
try: After 9:50 AM ET ask: "watch SOFI for an entry" (/trader-entry).

quiz.q: The trigger fired 45 minutes ago and the price has run 3 % higher. What does the bot's rule do?
choices: Skip it: too late to chase
quiz.why: An old trigger with a big run means a worse entry, a farther stop and a smaller target.

quiz.q: It is 3:40 PM and a chart just broke out. With the default cutoff, what happens?
choices: No new entry: the setup has expired
quiz.why: no_entries_after is 15:30 by default. Late entries have little time before flat by 15:55.

quiz.q: Why wait for the bar to close instead of buying the first tick above the high?
choices: A bar that pokes above can still close back inside the range
quiz.why: Waiting for the close filters out many false breaks, at the cost of a slightly later price.

lessons.title: Stops, targets and R
points: Set the stop and target BEFORE you enter, so nothing is decided in a fast move.
The stop is where the setup has failed. The default is the opening-range midpoint, rounded down to the cent.
R is your risk per share: entry minus stop. A 1R target is entry plus one R; 2R is entry plus two.
Reward to risk is (target minus entry) divided by (entry minus stop). A 1R target is 1:1.
A stop is a plan, not a guarantee. A gap or a halt can fill past it.
lessons.example: TSLA: range 354.47 to 362.18, midpoint 358.325, stop 358.32. Entry 364.18, so R = 5.86. 1R target = 370.04. Your own ENPH paper trade on Oct 29: entry about 25.24, stop 24.70, R = 0.54, target 25.78.
try: After an entry triggers ask: "set my stop and target" (/trader-exit).

quiz.q: Entry 50.00, stop 49.00. Where is the 2R target?
Entry 25.24, stop 24.70, target 25.78. What is the reward to risk?
quiz.why: Reward 0.54, risk 0.54: one to one, a 1R target.

quiz.q: Your stop is 24.70. The stock gaps down and opens at 24.10. Where can the stop fill?
quiz.why: A stop becomes a market order once hit; across a gap it fills near the next available price.

lessons.title: Position sizing: shares from your max loss
points: Size comes from risk, not from how much you like the chart. Shares = max loss per trade divided by R, rounded DOWN to whole shares.
Then the other limits: position cap, max order, cash after your buffer. The smallest one decides.
A stop too far away for your max loss is a refusal, not a smaller stop. Never move the stop to fit the size.
A common rule of thumb is to risk about 1 % of the account per trade.
lessons.example: Reel: $50 max loss / 5.86 = 8.53, so 8 TSLA shares ($2,913.44); loss at the stop $46.88. Yours: $10 max loss / 0.54 = 18.5, so 18 ENPH shares, about $454, loss at the stop $9.72.
try: After a plan is set ask: "how many shares" (/trader-budget). Ask "set my rules" to change your limits.

quiz.q: Max loss $10, entry 40.00, stop 39.20. How many whole shares?
quiz.why: R = 0.80. 10 / 0.80 = 12.5, rounded down to 12. The loss at the stop is $9.60.

quiz.q: Your max loss is $10 but the stop is $15 a share away. What does the Budget Manager do?
quiz.why: Even one share risks $15, over the $10 limit, so the trade is refused. Moving the stop would break the plan.

quiz.q: With a $1,000 budget, about what is a 1 % risk per trade?
quiz.why: 1 % of $1,000 is $10, the max loss you chose.

lessons.title: Daily limits: the rules that keep you in the game
points: Daily loss limit: once the day's losses (and open risk) reach it, no new trades until tomorrow. It stops one bad day becoming a disaster.
Trades per day: a cap stops revenge trading after a loss.
Entry window and flat by: no entries before 9:45 or after 15:30, everything closed by 15:55.
Getting out is never blocked. The limits only stop new risk.
The pattern day trader rule: if your broker still applies it, margin accounts under $25,000 are limited in day trades over 5 business days. pdt_guard counts them.
lessons.example: Your replay of Oct 28: after GMAB and BAC, a WULF trade was BLOCKED: $12.14 already at risk plus $9.99 = $22.13, over your $20 daily limit.
try: Ask: "how much have I risked today" or "check my order" (/trader-risk).

quiz.q: Daily limit $20. You have $12.14 at risk. A new trade risks $9.99. What happens?
quiz.why: 12.14 + 9.99 = 22.13, over the $20 daily loss limit.

quiz.q: You hit your daily loss limit while holding a position. Can you still sell it?
choices: Yes, getting out is never blocked
quiz.why: Limits stop new risk. Closing reduces risk, so it is always allowed.

quiz.q: What is a daily trade cap mainly protecting you from?
quiz.why: After a loss the urge to win it back fast is strong. A hard cap ends the day.

lessons.title: Odds, expectancy and why one day proves nothing
points: Expectancy in R: win rate times average win in R, minus loss rate times 1R. Above zero (after costs) is the only kind of edge.
Break-even win rate: with a 1R target you need over 50 % winners; with 2R, over 33.3 %, before costs.
The Time Machine replays the rest of the session 10,000 times from the stock's own recent bars, and re-runs the rule on every past day it fired. It is a reality check, not a promise.
Small samples lie. 5 trades can be all wins by luck. Judge a method on dozens of trades, not a day.
lessons.example: TSLA, Oct 19: target first 29.4 %, stop first 25.5 %, open at the close 45.1 %. On 33 real past firings: 13 targets, 15 stops, 5 neither. Verdict: close to a coin flip. Your Oct 28 replay made +$6.54 on 2 trades: far too few to mean anything.
try: After a plan is set ask: "run the time machine" (/trader-timemachine). Ask "replay the bot on yesterday" (/trader-bot).

quiz.q: 1R target, 55 % winners, 45 % losers, no costs. Expectancy per trade?
With a 2R target, roughly what win rate breaks even before costs?
quiz.why: p x 2 = (1 - p) x 1 gives p = 1/3.

quiz.q: The bot made money on its first day on paper. What does that tell you?
choices: Very little: one day is too small a sample
quiz.why: Luck dominates small samples. Keep it on paper and collect weeks of results.

lessons.title: Orders, brokers, the bot and keeping keys safe
points: Market order: fills now at the best price available. Limit: only at your price or better. Stop: becomes a market order once the stop price trades.
A bracket order is one entry with a stop-loss and a take-profit attached; when one leg fills, the other is cancelled.
/trader-broker places nothing without three yeses: risk passed that exact order, you typed yes in the chat, and you clicked Allow once on Claude's card.
The bot is the exception you switch on: it places its own bracket orders under your limits. Real money needs three separate switches. Its kill switch: say "stop the bot".
API keys are passwords. Never paste them into a chat. Put them only in your environment settings, and regenerate any key that was ever exposed.
lessons.example: Oct 29 2026, your paper bot: ECHO bracket (buy 5, stop 93.55, take-profit 97.01) hit its target and the stop leg was cancelled. ENPH bracket: buy 18, stop 24.70, take-profit 25.78.
try: Ask: "is the bot running" or "bot status" (/trader-bot). Ask "set up paper trading" (/trader-broker).

quiz.q: In a bracket order, the take-profit fills. What happens to the stop-loss leg?
quiz.why: The legs are one-cancels-other: the position is closed, so the stop is no longer needed.

quiz.q: Where should your Alpaca secret key go?
choices: Into the chat so Claude can use it
Into the config file in your project
quiz.why: Anything typed in a chat is stored in the history. Keys belong in environment variables only.

quiz.q: What does the bot need before it trades real money?
choices: Nothing, it is live by default
paper false in the config, --live on the command line and TRADER_BOT_LIVE=real-money, all three
quiz.why: Any two without the third is an error, never a fallback. Paper is the default everywhere.
